deep.reconstruction:
Left half. Grothendieck gives a correspondence of spaces Y <-p- Z -i-> X, with i a closed embedding in his picture. He defines a new 'space' 𝔛 by declaring that a sheaf on 𝔛 is a triple (F, G, α): F a sheaf on Y, G a sheaf on X, and α: p*F -> i*G a morphism, not necessarily an isomorphism. By adjunction α is the same as a map F -> p_* i* G. So Sh(𝔛) is the Artin gluing (comma topos) of Sh(Y) and Sh(X) along the left exact functor p_* i*: Sh(X) -> Sh(Y). In this topos Y is a closed subtopos and X is the open complement. He then writes down the standard functors.
- Closed embedding i': Y -> 𝔛: i'_*F = (F, 0, 0) and i'^*(F, G, α) = F.
- Open embedding p': X -> 𝔛: p'^*(F, G, α) = G, with right adjoint p'_*G = (p_* i* G, G, can), where can: p* p_* i* G -> i* G is the counit.
- Open embedding q: X - Z -> 𝔛: q_!G = (0, G, 0), meaning extension by zero. q^! is left blank.
Geometrically, 𝔛 is the topos of the space obtained by attaching the mapping cylinder of p to X along Z, i.e. a homotopy pushout of Y <- Z -> X. In this space Y sits as a closed stratum and X as an open 'tubular' piece. The time arrow goes from the closed part to the open part.

Right half. This explains the purpose. A stratified space X has strata indexed by a set Σ. One considers X_{I,J} = X_I - X_J for flags Σ ⊃ I ⊃ J, where J is subject to some condition (perhaps 'un crible'). There are maps α_{I,J/I',J'}: X_{I,J} -> X_{I',J'} between these pieces. There is a diagram ∂X_α -p_α-> (lower stratum), ∂X_α -i_α-> X_α. Here X_α is the stratum compactified as a manifold with boundary, and ∂X_α fibres over the adjacent strata via the tubular projection p_α. The program noted is:
- the six operations α_*, α^*, α_!, α^! for these maps;
- a dualizing complex K_{X,Λ}.
The gluing construction on the left is the elementary step. It reconstructs sheaves on a stratified (tame) space from sheaves on strata-with-boundary plus gluing maps along the boundary fibrations, i.e. a dévissage of a stratified space by successive 'mapping-cylinder' gluings. This context fits 'Topologie modérée', and the previous page mentions Abhyankar.
errors: q^!(G) is left blank. Since q is an open embedding, q^! = q^*, i.e. (F, G, α) |-> G|_{X-Z}.

q_!(G) = (0, G, 0) is slightly imprecise: G lives on X - Z, so the middle entry should be j_!G, with j: X - Z -> X. Also p'_!(G) = (0, G, 0) holds for G on X; it is not written but is the correct left adjoint.
No condition is stated making α an isomorphism. This is intended (lax gluing = comma topos), but it means 𝔛 is not the naive pushout X ∪_Z Y. It is the mapping-cylinder/homotopy pushout.

ideas.what: Sheaves on a space glued from a correspondence Y <- Z -> X described as triples (F, G, α: p*F -> i*G)
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing / comma topos; recollement; sheaves on a homotopy pushout (mapping cylinder)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier (SGA4 exp. IV, recollement/gluing of topoi); Wraith (Artin glueing, 1974); Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne for triangulated recollement

ideas.what: Explicit formulas for i'_*, i'^*, p'^*, p'_*, q_! on the glued topos
ideas.modern_name: Six-functor formalism for an open–closed decomposition

ideas.what: Dévissage of a stratified space into pieces X_{I,J} = X_I - X_J (flags Σ ⊃ I ⊃ J), strata as manifolds with boundary ∂X_α fibred over lower strata, with six operations and dualizing complex K_{X,Λ}
ideas.modern_name: Stratified spaces with control data / 'dévissage' of tame stratified spaces; constructible sheaves via exit paths; Verdier duality on stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data), Goresky–MacPherson, MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie (exit paths), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (conically smooth decollements)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, dévissage of stratified structures) in outline only

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses lax Artin gluing along a tubular correspondence (lower stratum <- boundary of the stratum's compactification -> compactified stratum) as the basic building block for sheaf theory on tame stratified spaces. He intends to run a full six-operation/duality formalism over the poset of pieces X_{I,J}. This anticipates the later 'stratified spaces as iterated gluings/decollements' approach to constructible sheaves (Treumann, Lurie HA A.9, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka) inside his 1974 'topologie modérée' notes.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: an early (1974) sketch linking the Esquisse tame-topology dévissage with gluing of topoi and duality. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The gluing formulas are routine SGA4 recollement. The interest is the early 1974 context: Grothendieck sketches a six-functor/duality formalism for tame stratified spaces built by iterated mapping-cylinder gluings along boundary fibrations. This prefigures the Esquisse dévissage and later exit-path/decollement work, but it is only an outline.
transcription_corrections: First entry of q_!(G) is written like ∅/0 (slashed circle), i.e. 0.
The line under 'Σ ⊃ I ⊃ J' is barely legible. 'J un cristal' is doubtful; possibly 'J un crible' (a sieve in the stratification poset) with a condition on elements of J.
In the diagram, the arrow from ∂X_α labelled p_α points to a crossed-out target. i_α: ∂X_α -> X_α is vertical.
Above the arrow X_{I,J} -> X_{I',J'} the label is α_{I,J/I',J'}.
